name: Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of broad and angulated thumbs and halluces
Characteristic facial features including downslanting palpebral fissures, beaked nose, and grimacing smile
Mild to moderate intellectual disability or developmental delay
Pathogenic variant in CREBBP or EP300 genes
Postnatal growth retardation or short stature

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of broad thumbs/halluces, distinctive facial features, and intellectual disability; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for CREBBP or EP300 mutations is confirmatory but not always required if clinical features are definitive

pathognomonic.symptomName: Broad and angulated thumbs and halluces
searchTerms: wide and bent thumbs and big toes
thick and crooked thumb and big toe

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distinctive facial dysmorphism (beaked nose, downslanting palpebral fissures, grimacing smile)
searchTerms: distinct facial features like hooked nose

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intellectual disability ranging from mild to moderate

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., patent ductus arteriosus, atrial septal defect)
Ocular abnormalities including strabismus and refractive errors
searchTerms: eye problems including crossed eyes and vision errors
ocular abnormalities like misaligned eyes and refractive issues
unusual tooth shape like extra cusps
renal swelling due to urine buildup

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers
Possible mild anemia or thrombocytopenia in some cases
imaging: Skeletal X-rays showing broad thumbs and halluces
Brain MRI may show nonspecific findings or structural abnormalities
Echocardiography to detect congenital heart defects
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CREBBP gene (~50-60% cases)
Pathogenic variants in EP300 gene (~5-10% cases)

distinguishingFeatures: Distinctive synophrys and limb abnormalities different from broad thumbs
Different facial features such as arched eyebrows
Speech delay more prominent than intellectual disability

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects requiring urgent intervention
Progressive respiratory compromise due to recurrent infections
references: Hennekam RC. Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome. Eur J Hum Genet. 2006;14(9):981-5.
Petrij F, et al. Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome caused by mutations in the transcriptional co-activator CBP. Nature. 1995;376(6538):348-51.
Roelfsema JH, Peters DJ. Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome: clinical and molecular overview. Expert Rev Mol Med. 2007;9(23):1-16.
